newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili, in Atlantic, heads towards Europe.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili, in Atlantic, heads towards Europe.

text.p: Hurricane Lili grew in strength as it swirled in the open Atlantic on Thursday and forecasters said it could bring heavy winds and rains to Europe within four or five days.

At 5 p.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the hurricane's centre was near latitude 34.2 north and longitude 51.0 west, or about 1,265 miles (2,035 km) west-southwest of the Azores, and moving east-northeast at about seven mph (11 kph), the National Hurricane Centre said.
That motion was expected to continue through Friday, it added.
"The hurricane is supposed to become a winter storm in 36 hours," said hurricane specialist Lexion Avila. "In four or five days it might be near England."
Maximum sustained winds, fluctuating since Wednesday, increased to 85 mph (140 kph) at 5 p.m., but some weakening was expected during the next 24 hours as the storm moved over cooler waters.
Forecasters noted that Lili had been a hurricane for seven days, and said this was unusual for late October. The six-month Atlantic hurricane season ends on Nov. 30.
Lili formed off the coast of Central America last week, spawning high winds and flooding that was blamed for 10 deaths in Nicaragua, Honduras and Costa Rica.
It hit Cuba a week ago, causing extensive damage to agriculture and making thousands homeless, and then headed east to wreak havoc in the central Bahamas with 90 mph (145 kph) winds.
